title: LASSO identifies a three-gene signature associated with colorectal-cancer prognosis
summary: LASSO selection of dephosphorylation-related candidates from TCGA colorectal-cancer data produced a SNAI1/TCF7L1/TIMP1 survival-risk signature. Prognostic analysis used 524 TCGA cases and 55 GSE17537 cases; reported 1-, 2- and 3-year AUCs were 0.604/0.626/0.658 in training and 0.687/0.764/0.652 in validation. New expression measurements in five paired tumors/adjacent tissues supported higher tumor SNAI1 and higher adjacent-tissue TCF7L1; TIMP1 did not differ significantly. These measurements do not validate survival prediction. The preprint reports retrospective associations and computational treatment-response estimates; phosphatase-dependent mechanisms, clinical utility and observed treatment benefit remain unestablished.
organization: The Third Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University

evidence.tested: 524 survival-annotated TCGA colorectal tumors and 55 GSE17537 cases evaluated the three-gene signature. RT-qPCR in five paired clinical tissues assessed expression, not prognostic validity.
evidence.unknown: Associational retrospective result; no causal phosphatase mechanism, prospective survival model validation or confirmed treatment-response prediction. Small external cohort and selected cutoff limit transfer.
evidence.ai_role: After differential-expression and Cox/proportional-hazards screening, LASSO with 10-fold cross-validation selected nonzero prognostic features for a Cox risk signature.

source_review.scope: Research Square v1 full 41-page PDF: data collection/feature-selection/evaluation Methods, model and expression Results, Discussion/limitations; cover posting date 2026-11-20. No supplement or independent validation.
